section_1.title: The Concept of Transformation
section_1.content: Define linear transformation as a mapping between vector spaces that preserves vector addition and scalar multiplication. Introduce the grid system as a visual anchor.
section_1.example: Imagine a 2D grid of dots. A transformation acts like a stretchy rubber sheet that moves these dots while keeping the grid lines straight and the origin fixed.

section_2.title: Basis Vectors: The Building Blocks
section_2.content: Explain that any transformation can be fully described by where the basis vectors i-hat (1,0) and j-hat (0,1) land after the transformation occurs.
section_2.example: Visualize i-hat (red arrow) moving to (2, 0) and j-hat (green arrow) moving to (0, 2). This shows a uniform scaling effect.

section_3.title: From Transformation to Matrix
section_3.content: Demonstrate how the coordinates of the moved basis vectors are packed into the columns of a matrix. This bridges the gap between geometry and algebra.
section_3.example: Using the previous movement: i-hat lands at [2, 0] and j-hat at [0, 2]. These become the columns of the matrix: [[2, 0], [0, 2]].

section_4.title: Practical Application: Graphic Engines
section_4.content: Show how matrices are used in game design to rotate or scale characters. Highlight that matrix-vector multiplication is the engine behind 3D rendering.
section_4.example: A game developer wants to rotate a character by 90 degrees. They apply a rotation matrix to the character's vertex coordinates, instantly transforming the character's position on screen.

section_5.title: Conclusion and Summary
section_5.content: Recap: A matrix is not just a block of numbers; it is a geometric instruction for space. Matrix multiplication is simply the composition of two geometric transformations.
section_5.example: Summarize with an animation of a square being stretched into a rectangle, then sheared into a parallelogram, represented by the product of two matrices.

from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(f"- {line}", font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (6x6 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 1.0 + j * 0.8
                y = 2.0 - i * 0.8
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("From Transformation to Matrix", [
            "Where basis vectors land defines the transformation matrix.",
            "The coordinates become columns of the new matrix.",
            "This maps geometry directly into algebraic form."
        ])
        
        # Matrix Setup
        matrix = Matrix([[2, 0], [0, 2]])
        self.place_at_grid(matrix, 'C3', scale_factor=1.2)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#FFFFFF"))
        self.play(Create(matrix))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#FFFF00"))
        # Highlighting the columns
        column1_rect = SurroundingRectangle(matrix.get_columns()[0], color=YELLOW)
        column2_rect = SurroundingRectangle(matrix.get_columns()[1], color=YELLOW)
        self.play(Create(column1_rect))
        self.wait(0.5)
        self.play(ReplacementTransform(column1_rect, column2_rect))
        self.wait(0.5)

        self.play(Write(map_text))

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Basis vectors define the entire coordinate system.",
            "Observe i-hat at (1,0) and j-hat at (0,1).",
            "The transformation tracks where these basis vectors land."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Basis Vectors: The Building Blocks", lecture_lines)
        
        # Setup grid and vectors

        j_hat = Vector(UP, color=GREEN)
        
        i_hat_label = MathTex(r"\hat{i}", color=GREEN).next_to(i_hat, DOWN)
        j_hat_label = MathTex(r"\hat{j}", color=GREEN).next_to(j_hat, LEFT)

        basis_group = VGroup(i_hat, j_hat, i_hat_label, j_hat_label).move_to(axes.c2p(0,0))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#00FF00"))
        self.play(Create(axes), Create(basis_group))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#0000FF"))
        grid = NumberPlane(x_range=[-1, 3, 1], y_range=[-1, 3, 1]).scale(0.5).move_to(axes.get_center())

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#FF00FF"))
        
        # Transformation: i_hat to (2,0), j_hat to (0,2)
        new_i_hat = Vector(2*RIGHT, color=RED)
        new_j_hat = Vector(2*UP, color=RED)
        
        self.play(
            ReplacementTransform(i_hat, new_i_hat),
            ReplacementTransform(j_hat, new_j_hat),
            run_time=2
        )
        self.wait(1)

from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Practical Application: Graphic Engines", [
            "Matrices act as engines for computer graphics.",
            "They rotate and scale vertices in real-time.",
            "Multiplication enables smooth character movement in games."
        ])
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Show a 2D shape in a coordinate system. Color #FFFFFF.
        shape = Square(side_length=1.5, color=WHITE)
        self.place_at_grid(shape, 'C3')
        self.play(Create(shape))
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FFFFFF")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Apply matrix transformation to shape vertices. Color #FF9900.
        matrix = [[0, -1], [1, 0]] # 90 degree rotation
        rotated_shape = shape.copy().set_color("#FF9900")
        rotated_shape.apply_matrix(matrix)
        
        self.play(Transform(shape, rotated_shape))
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#FF9900")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Animate rendering the transformed shape frames. Color #00FF00.
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#00FF00")
        self.play(shape.animate.set_color("#00FF00").shift(RIGHT * 1))
        self.wait(1)
